claims.text: Untreated nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts have a homogeneous metallic surface.
Untreated catalysts lack an engineered surface oxide layer.
Controlled electrochemical potential cycling can induce a reproducible thin oxide layer on the catalyst surface.
The induced oxide layer is tunable, self-limiting, and passivating.
Formation of the surface oxide alters the surface electronic structure.
Formation of the surface oxide alters the catalyst's adsorption characteristics.
The oxide layer protects the catalyst against degradation during ethanol oxidation.
The oxide layer fine-tunes the binding energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Optimized intermediate adsorption and desorption kinetics allow activity to be maintained while rapid deactivation is prevented.
Oxide-treated catalysts will exhibit slower activity decay than untreated catalysts.
Oxide-treated catalysts will retain higher current density during extended cycling than untreated catalysts.
Operando spectroscopy will detect a consistent and reproducible thin oxide layer whose presence correlates with improved durability.
The proposed protective-oxide mechanism should hold at room temperature in acidic aqueous electrolyte over a potential-cycling window of 0.1–1.2 V versus RHE.
Conditions substantially outside 0.1–1.2 V versus RHE may not produce the same protective oxide.
